previous_audits.chain_closure_explanation: The kernel sends any row-law p to (1-alpha)p+alpha pi, so subtracting pi gives pK-pi=(1-alpha)(p-pi), which proves the displayed iterate by induction. Averaging the geometric series over t=0,...,N-1 gives the finite-N expected frequency formula with the stated factor.
previous_audits.claim_scope: Given a finite normalized supplied prior pi, supplied initial law p0, supplied 0<alpha<1, and reset kernel K(i,j)=(1-alpha)delta_ij+alpha pi_j, the note derives the exact finite-N ensemble expected empirical frequency and keeps realized counts integral.
previous_audits.load_bearing_step: For K(i,j)=(1-alpha)delta_ij+alpha pi_j, the iterates satisfy p_t=pi+(1-alpha)^t(p0-pi), hence E[f_N]=pi+((1-(1-alpha)^N)/(N alpha))(p0-pi).
previous_audits.notes_for_re_audit_if_any: A second auditor should re-check only that downstream status does not overread this as deriving pi, alpha, p0, concentration, a clock/rate, Born law, or physical dynamics.

The displayed identities have the correct sign, normalization, and geometric-series factor: the row-stochastic reset kernel preserves normalization and contracts p-pi by 1-alpha each event step. The runner source genuinely computes the kernel, iterates it, compares against the closed form, checks target dependence, and separately verifies the firewall text; it does not hard-code the contested formula as its only support.
